apiEndpoints.summary: Returns aggregated behavioral, funnel, matching, and geospatial telemetry powered by Orazaka Data Analysis and local high-velocity clustering.
The audit log for the console — sign-ins, password changes, suspensions, restorations, deletions — searched, filtered and paged on the server.
Reads the active dynamic configuration for the Admin Customization Studio.
Updates the dynamic customization without redeploying code.
Lists all administrative geofencing zones.
Creates a new geofenced zone.
The instance's health for the console: database, realtime bus, version, environment, uptime, whether sign-up is open.
The introductions overview for the console — state, dates, message counts; never who said what — filtered and paged on the server.
The console's overview: accounts by status, the moderation queue, introductions by state, open batches — counts only.
The moderation queue for the console — urgent reasons (UNDERAGE, THREAT) first while open — filtered by status and paged on the server; details open one report at a time.
One report with its details opened — operators only.
Moves a report along (REVIEWED · ACTIONED · DISMISSED, or back to OPEN); the decision is logged with who made it.
The reports for operators — urgent reasons (UNDERAGE, THREAT) first, details decrypted; service token and IP allow-list.
Lists accounts for the console — searched by address or name, filtered by status and role, sorted and paged on the server.
Law 25 erasure of an account, asked of an operator; the e-mail typed confirms.
One account for the console: state, role, counts and the audit lines about it — never a date of birth, a message or a photo.
Lifts an account's suspension: it is ACTIVE again and can sign in; the restoration is logged.
Grants or withdraws the administrator role.
Ends every session of an account, on the web and in the app, leaving it active.
Suspends an account: it cannot sign in and every session of the app and the browser ends at once; the reason is logged.
The person's agent: the conversation, what it understood in their own words, the portrait once written, what it still has to learn.
Says something to the agent and gets its answer; what the agent understood of it follows (extraction, then the portrait when it knows enough).
Signs out: forgets this phone's push token, and with `everywhere` invalidates every session token of the account at once (the app also deletes its own token from secure storage).
Signs a person in to the web console with their e-mail and password: the answer sets an HttpOnly session cookie.
"Forgot password": a reset code by e-mail, the same answer whether an account exists or not.
The code and the new password.
Sends a 6-digit sign-in code to an e-mail address — the same answer whether an account exists or not.
Signs the web console out: this browser's session ends and its cookie is cleared (an unknown cookie is cleared too).
Exchanges an e-mail code for a session token (`client: "native"`, sent back as `Authorization: Bearer`).
Opens the person's next batch — three to five people who fit both ways — once the agent has written their portrait; 409 `NO_FIT_YET` when nobody does.
The batch the person has to answer: who is in it, why you two in words both ways, until when — never a score.
The people the account blocked (the settings list), oldest first.
Blocks someone — immediate, invisible to them, mutual in effect: their intro closes and each leaves the other's current batch.
Lifts one of the account's blocks (what it closed stays closed); another account's block is a 404.
Public client configuration endpoint: returns active design tokens, branding, matching thresholds, and feature flags dynamically for both Web and Mobile apps.

The account's live events as Server-Sent Events — `batch.ready`, `intro.opened`, `intro.message` (ids only: the app fetches what changed) — with a heartbeat every 15 s, ending every 5 minutes (the app reconnects at once).
Health of this instance: the database answers (503 when it does not) and whether the realtime bus hears the other instances.

Deletes the account for good, at once — every row that is theirs, in one transaction; the photos are purged from storage right after (retried until done, 30 days at most) and a confirmation e-mail leaves.
The signed-in account: e-mail, status, language, age (never the date of birth), profile, rounded position, the agent's state.
Changes the profile, the language, or pauses the account (nobody is shown it any more; its batches and intros stay open).
The signed-in account's home: where the agent is, the open batch, the introductions, the phones — counts and dates, never a person's profile or a score.
Everything the account holds, as JSON — at once when it takes under a second, else 202 with an export id to poll (`?id=`, kept 24 hours); `?mode=async` asks for the background build directly.
Sets the position from the phone's coordinates, rounded to about 1 km before it is written — the exact one is never stored; the answer is what was kept.
Changes the account's password (the current one must be right); every other browser session of the account ends.
The account's own photos in their order, with status, size and blurhash — never a URL (GET /api/photos/{id} signs one).
Reorders the photos: `order` lists each of the account's photos once, the first one first.
Starts a photo: declares its type and size and answers a signed upload URL (PUT, 300 seconds, this photo only); then `PUT /api/me/photos/{id}/complete`.
Removes one of the account's photos — from storage first, then from the profile (another account's photo is a 404).

Completes an upload: checks the bytes are the declared picture, re-encodes them (orientation applied, metadata — GPS included — stripped), computes width, height and blurhash, then moderation (V1: approved automatically).
Ends every other browser session of the account (the one making the call stays).
The signed-in account's browser sessions — where they are signed in, since when, last used — the current one marked.
Ends one browser session of the account; ending the current one signs this browser out.

apiEndpoints.access: signed media URL (300 s, development storage only)
apiEndpoints.summary: Development storage only: serves a local photo at a URL `GET /api/photos/{id}` signed (300 seconds, one width) — what Bunny's pull zone and Optimizer do in production.

A photo for the signed-in viewer — after the access rule (its owner; someone with the owner in a current batch; an open intro), a URL signed for 300 seconds at the asked width (`?w=`, snapped to 160…1280).
Forgets this phone's push token (notifications turned off on the device).
Registers this phone's Expo push token for the account (a phone that changed hands moves to the new account).
Reports someone, with a normalised reason — persisted before it is acknowledged, the details encrypted at rest, a report inside an intro freezes it.

Receives one photo's bytes at the URL `POST /api/me/photos` signed — the signature is the authorisation (one photo, 300 seconds); the type must be the declared one and the size at most the declared one.
